s1.syndrome_frame: Painful erosive skin lesion around a stoma site with suprabasal epidermal splitting and acantholysis
salient_findings: Painful, erosive lesion around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
Suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis on histopathology
Intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis on direct immunofluorescence
key_facts: Patient has a 10-year history of Crohn disease
Patient underwent total proctocolectomy and ileostomy
Painful, erosive lesion developed 5 weeks after surgery
Lesion is located around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
Repeated microbiological cultures were negative
Histopathology showed epidermal erosion with suprabasal epidermal splitting and acantholysis
Direct immunofluorescence showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 were detected

raw.rationale: The presence of suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis, intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout the epidermis, and high levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 are characteristic of Pemphigus vulgaris.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: Typically associated with underlying neoplasms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
rejected.why: Characterized by subcorneal blistering and autoantibodies against desmoglein 1, but not desmoglein 3

rejected.label: Pemphigus herpetiformis
rejected.why: A variant of pemphigus with a different clinical and histological presentation, not matching the described suprabasal epidermal splitting and autoantibody profile

rejected.label: Pemphigus herpetiformis variant with IgG and C3 deposition
rejected.why: Although it shares some features, the presence of high levels of autoantibodies against both desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 and the clinical context better fit Pemphigus vulgaris
